notes: The reconstructed action and driving engines are the game's own code from the pinned nightfire-cxbx revision, patched only for the Apple port; the supplied Xbox image and both XBEs are the game itself.
Campaign and multiplayer systems are preserved in source and inventoried; runtime acceptance stays under R09 and R17.
tests/test_data_tools.py now covers the listing validation, BIGF/RefPack readers and the CARP track inspector, and verify_quick runs it.
Preflight, staging, validation, cancellation, atomic activation, replacement and rollback retention are covered by scripts/test_data_import.sh.
The shell imports a prepared tree from the picker or from Documents/NightPad Import with progress and cancel, and re-import leaves Saves byte-identical.
Choosing an arbitrary external folder still uses the system picker and is manual in this harness.
Startup cleanup removes stage trees left by earlier imports; a 7.6 GB pile in the simulator fell to the single active tree.
The device shell links the combined action and driving engines with static SDL, FFmpeg and SPIRV-Cross; the IPA is arm64 with only system libraries.
A signed install and run on physical hardware, without a debugger or JIT, is the remaining proof.
Simulator pointer/Metal/media probes pass; macOS action, driving and mixed ten-cycle gates pass. Physical device execution remains blocked.
Cooperative stop, worker and file-slot shutdown, heap re-arm, explicit session-static reset and GPU-cache reset pass ten action, ten driving and ten mixed cycles.

Names/order, start levels, chains, media coverage, difficulty/failure structure and missing-intro tolerance are inventoried; NTSC matches the supplied 30 fps bundle. Runs and completion evidence remain.
Campaign order, level parts, objectives and media are inventoried; the action and driving engines both boot missions on the host and the action-driving-action transition passes.
A full first-play route from a fresh codename through the ending, with saves and relaunch, needs a device.
Host gates show action SFX and streams paused and resumed with frames held, and the driving sound manager paused and resumed; movies play in the handoff gate.
Device interruptions (calls, route changes, audio focus) and sustained synchronization under load are unverified.

The engine writes through a durable Saves link; Share Saves exports via the system sheet and Import Saves copies chosen files back with a replace confirmation. Picker selection, a real in-game save and the app-update case remain.
An app reinstall (the simulator update path) kept the save, settings file, touch layout and imported tree byte-identical.
Save restore now writes atomically, so an interrupted restore keeps the previous file; the fixture hook proved the collision prompt, replacement and unrelated-file isolation.
Touch layout, editor, overlay, simultaneous mapping, app settings (including older files without newer keys) and accessibility pass their checks. Physical ergonomics remain.
The engine keeps its schemes and preferences; help separates Driving from Mounted views and names the POV variations across eight configurations. In-game checks remain.
All eight action schemes are mapped from psiInput.cpp with their differences from Nightfire recorded in docs/CONTROL-SCHEMES.md.

Four-port mixer, touch mapping, GameController authority, slot reconciliation, per-port rumble, host-pad override and touch auto-hide owned by port 0 are implemented. Physical connect/reconnect and a real second controller remain.

The three-dot menu, editor and data panels are recoverable; native UI pauses the engine and suspends input. Both engines now prove audio pause/resume in their gates. Hearing it and the full device path remain.
Background pause/foreground resume follows a tested rule that preserves native-UI and player pauses. Memory-warning, surface recreation and device suspension remain.
Limits, modes, maps, weapon sets, Enviro-Mods, map rules, unlock matrix, match rules and bot setup options are inventoried. Match execution and physical ports remain.

Render scale, FXAA, widescreen and vertical FOV (60/70/80) are exposed, persisted and written to the engine; host runs at 1x-3x reach the same cap. Aspect/HUD/scope checks and device performance remain.
Secret Unlocks has 52 codes in five families applied to the edited codename; mechanism and device test plan recorded. Physical entry/persistence remains.
The reconstructed debug table is audited with a per-option product decision; only immortality and unlimited ammo are exposed, off by default and excluded from acceptance runs.
All-weapons equip is deferred with a concrete blocker: it needs player 0 to exist and the standalone harness cannot boot a live level. Unlock-everything is rejected because it bypasses progression.
D3D9-only DDS replacement; SDL/Metal port planned but deferred because no Xbox texture pack scene exists.
Source has no networking layer and the front-end exposes only local multiplayer. Two approaches analysed; both are out of scope without source support, so online play is deferred.
Netplay is deferred, so two-device consistency and impairment testing do not apply.
Measurement routes, provisional budgets and a PerfLog summarizer are in place; no device measurement has run.
Reports carry app/build identity, data and engine state, display options, assist state and session events, with paths and credential-looking values redacted; nothing is uploaded.
The Release lane reports build_configuration=performance/release, and test_release_diagnostics.sh boots and shuts down one simulator to read it.
Patch provenance, a clean shell build and an unsigned device IPA recipe pass. Signing/install and a full clean-checkout rebuild of engine and dependencies remain.
scripts/test_clean_shell_build.sh rebuilt both lanes from empty trees at 5b8583a and the link check passed; the unsigned package was rebuilt at the same commit.
scripts/check_package.sh verifies the IPA contents, arm64 slice, system-only linkage and the required Info.plist keys; the package script runs it.
Donor notices and pins live in UPSTREAM-DELTA and dependencies.lock; the upstream engine has no reviewed first-party license, which PROVENANCE records as an open distribution question.
scripts/check_privacy.sh fails on retail, binary or private trees and on any networking API in apple/.
scripts/verify_engine.sh passed in full on commit 480ac5a: action and driving lifecycles, action and driving pause with audio, assists, driving early stop, transition, handoff and round trip.
scripts/verify_quick.sh covers the host unit tests, both shell lanes, the link contract, patch provenance and privacy.
Device-only scenarios and the missing PAL media are listed as explicit blockers in docs/TEST-MATRIX.md rather than assumed.
Labels, 44-point controls, Dynamic Type, 4.5:1 contrast and explicit overlay/editor reading order are verified in the simulator. Physical VoiceOver remains.
All shell labels now opt into Dynamic Type; the data panel and About render at XXL with the card still fitting.
The monospaced titles and the diagnostics report now scale through UIFontMetrics; the report and About stay scrollable at XXL.
The manifest draft and identity script cover the whole pinned graph (five checkouts), lock/patch hashes, data/content and package hashes, and refuse an uncommitted freeze. Device results remain.

journal_entries.summary: Loop activated; pinned sources, toolchain and ownership boundaries recorded.
Supplied image deduplicated, hashed and listed; required trees present.
Native baseline built; replay and iOS simulator probes reached their content/device boundaries.
Both full engines compile for iPhoneOS and their isolated objects link in one executable with two bridge symbols.
Added opt-in in-process launch request seam; page and requesting thread verified without child process.
Switched iOS engine builds to static SDL; standalone and combined arm64 links pass without a loose SDL dylib dependency.
Bound FFmpeg statically in both iOS engines and preserved the native dynamic path; native 635-frame smoke still passes.
Shared GameWindow/HostPosix allocator runtime fixes the symbolized shader heap crash; worker-thread leak remains.
Three isolated action start/stop cycles pass with a shared allocator; surviving threads identified as Cocoa/GCD pool and stable.
Driving start and cleanup work; cross-engine launch request captures page but hangs before join.
Fault was missing window quit in driving stop plus join-before-close ordering; driving one-cycle lifecycle now joins.
Page-driven combined harness added; driving boots into shader 7 then crashes when both isolated engines are linked.
Combined crash localized to load-time engine initialization/MEM_size, not shader translation.
Enumerated combined mod-init tables; common sdlGpuBackend constructor runs twice and leads the static-init conflict.
Lazy Fmv/LaunchOptions singletons fixed combined load-time conflict; page-driven driving-to-action transition passes.
Reverse action->driving transition passes through psiLaunchDriving; combined harness is bidirectional.
One bidirectional cycle passes; repeated driving start faults after main, isolating mutable engine global reset.
Kernel initialization guarded once; SDL persistence experiment reverted after driving join regression.
Reverse trigger now uses Boot_GetPTPData; repeated driving start still fails, ruling out malformed page.
Session-scoped heap/static reset and in-window thread stacks make three driving and three mixed cycles pass; ten action cycles still grow Metal graphics memory.
Ten action, driving and mixed cycles pass with stable joins and plateauing memory; G04 now waits only on physical-device evidence.
Added explicit app paths and a transactional prepared-data import core with cancellation, validation, atomic activation and save separation.
Added the native shell target with persistent three-dot menu, data import/status panel, pause/about/diagnostics surfaces; simulator and device builds pass.
Linked the combined engine archive into the iPhoneOS shell and added an engine-host wrapper that prepares private settings; live window and pause wiring remain.
Added a nonblocking SDL poll bridge and wired shell Start/Stop with a transparent overlay above the engine window; device runtime and pause gating remain.
Added cooperative engine pause with audio suspension, shell App Pause/Back to Game wiring, and a passing frame-stop/resume test.
Suspended pad/keyboard/pointer input while native UI is open and tied it to shell menu/pause surfaces; device builds pass.
Added a reviewable local diagnostics report with path/credential redaction and explicit share; simulator review and device build pass.
Verified the reviewed diagnostic report reaches the system share sheet and is written privately under Logs/NightPad with redaction.
Added a native About page with source/donor links and independence/game-data notices; builds and simulator rendering pass.
Shell imported a synthetic prepared folder through real validation/activation, persisted the active identity across relaunch and preserved saves.
Added and tested a four-port Xbox input mixer with source merging, tap edges, dead zones, triggers and release-before-reacquire.
Added a versioned normalized touch-layout model with independent phone/tablet defaults, clamping, reset and atomic persistence.
Menu actions now defer sheet presentation until the UIMenu dismisses; alerts use the same route, and layout rebuilds keep hidden controls invisible to VoiceOver.
Resolved the extra front-end headings: they are campaign chapters inside the twelve wheel missions, not selectable entries, and the engine never references them.
Inventoried the objectives of all 24 action level parts from MissionData, which also identifies the two cut chapters by their placeholder objectives.
Documented how each mission part starts and ends: per-part objective reset, first-part stats reset, outro routing for final parts and the four failure channels.
Mission progress is saved from the results page with SAVE_ALL, not by any level part, so failure and death lose the run.
The touch editor can hide or show a control from a long-press menu; the flag round-trips and the live overlay omits hidden controls.
Refreshed the draft candidate identity and rebuilt the unsigned IPA on the current clean tree; final freeze still needs device acceptance.
Checked the tablet touch defaults and live overlay on an iPad simulator; iPad sheet saving and drag editing remain open.
Added Import from NightPad Folder for Documents/NightPad Import and made both import paths show the data panel with progress and Cancel Import.
Decided R21: the engine DDS replacement is D3D9-only, the SDL backend has no hook, and no Xbox texture pack scene exists; prototype deferred with a plan.
Filled the empty R01 and R28 records: foundation provenance for R01, and a full current-tree engine suite (verify_engine PASS) plus explicit device/media blockers for R28.

Closed R04, R20, R25 and R27 against existing evidence: transactional import with progress and cancel, the audited cheat decision, local diagnostics with distinct builds, and the provenance/privacy boundary.
The data panel import button now offers the system picker and the NightPad folder side by side, and the folder path works from the panel with progress and cancel.
Verified that an app reinstall keeps saves, settings, touch layout and imported game data byte-identical; only interrupted engine writes and a signed store update remain for R11.
Save restore writes atomically and is now driven end to end by a fixture hook: collision prompt, exact contents, unrelated files untouched.
Device handoff checklist updated for the app-folder import, save restore, control hiding and the rebuilt package; candidate snapshot refreshed.
Added Restore Saves from NightPad Folder so save restore no longer needs the system picker; verified contents, collision prompt and isolation from unrelated files.
Clean shell rebuild and package reproduction re-verified at 5b8583a; handoff and candidate manifests carry the new package hash.
Deferred presentations now wait for the window and alerts stack, so a corrupt settings file and a corrupt layout are both reported instead of one being lost.
Mapped the eight action control schemes from psiInput.cpp, documented the differences from Nightfire, and named them in Control Help.
Located the driving objective strings in data/gfx/locale inside misc.viv and documented the table format; per-mission attribution still needs the track event parser.
Collected the open issues and the apparent-but-expected behaviours into docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md for the candidate handoff.
Tried a headless objective log: Mission 1 loads and runs but never posts an objective without driving input, so attribution needs the track parser or a driven run. The hook was reverted.
Holding throttle through the host-pad hook for 30s and 90s still produced no objective message; headless attribution is ruled out and the experimental hooks were reverted.
The touch editor exposes per-control opacity through a long-press submenu; the value applies live and persists in the layout file.
Sheets now report interactive dismissal, so swiping a sheet away clears native UI instead of leaving the game flagged paused; unsaved editor changes are dropped like Cancel.
The data panel now shows the data state and identity itself, since the home status label is hidden behind it.
The home status label hides while the data panel is open, so the panel is the only status surface and nothing shows through the card.
The Game Data & Saves panel now offers Share Saves and Restore Saves beside import, with restore refused while the engine runs.
The panel's Restore button now offers the system picker and the Save Import folder, matching the import row.
Session history now records a resume only when native UI actually held the game, and interactive dismissal logs its own sheet-dismissed event.
Added a package content check (three entries, arm64, system libraries only, minimum OS, landscape, file sharing) and wired it into the packaging script; manifests carry the rebuilt hash.
Missing Dynamic Type opt-ins were added across the shell and diagnostics; the data panel and About render at XXL.
Abandoned import stage trees are removed at startup, freeing 7.6 GB in the simulator while keeping the active tree and saves.
Old identity trees left by importing different content are removed at launch, keeping only the active identity; the host test covers the rule.
Leftover-tree cleanup moved to a utility queue at launch, so multi-gigabyte deletes no longer block the first frame; planted leftovers were gone within three seconds.
Refreshed STATUS: current outcome, timestamp and next-step list, including the driving-objective attribution as the open source item.
Filled the empty R09 and R10 records with the existing campaign inventory and host audio-pause evidence; both remain in progress pending device runs.
Filled R05 with the device-link, package and arm64 evidence it already had, leaving the signed hardware run as the open part.
The home and About titles and the diagnostics report now scale through UIFontMetrics; the report is readable and scrollable at XXL.
A MakeEvent-time objective log also produced nothing: the track creates those events only when the mission reaches that stage. The hook was reverted; three headless routes are ruled out.

A 180-second event-hook run still produced no objective: the direct -mission boot takes the EU PAL default, misses paris_intro, and starts its main loop a minute in. The harness default is now recorded; the hook was reverted.
Added a CARP track inspector that decodes the map group and rule event lists; Paris objective events have empty comments, so the text lives in another event family.

The driving missions name their description and hints in loading-screen layouts, not objective comments; the five missions and their ids are inventoried, and resolving them needs the locale index decoded.
Resolved the driving missions descriptions and hints through the engine during headless boots and wrote the paraphrased goals into the campaign inventory; the temporary hook was reverted.
The data tools finally run in verify_quick, and the track inspector has a synthetic-CARP test.
Added --open-pause so the App Pause card can be inspected without an engine; it renders and scales, and the home status label stays hidden under it.
Moved the active goal to the candidate handoff and refreshed the next-step text: the campaign and driving inventories are complete, so only device acceptance and the multiplayer matrix remain.
Added scripts/freeze_candidate.sh: a clean-tree check, the gates, a fresh package and the identity in one command, logged to build/package/candidate.txt.
Moved the freeze log out of build/package and ran the full freeze: quick gates, engine suite PASS, package and identity all captured in build/candidate.txt.
Verified the handoff preflight: it builds the unsigned device shell, reports no connected devices and prints the install command. All remaining work needs hardware.
